I was also concerned, at that time, about commercial appropriations of technology that I had developed but had not patented. Now, sixteen years later, that is no longer a fear, and I would like to share the drawings and diagrams of each optical set-up that was used to make "Event Horizon". 

Had he shared would light art be more well know and common as others could have built on his techniuqe in the last sixteen year?

I feel, and have always felt, and have expressed my concern that holography will not grow until holographers get together and share their technique and findings. It's no wonder the newby makes a hologam of a figurine instead of dazzeling 3-dimensional light display. JMHO.

posts.content_md:
I'm not sure if this reply is most appropriate for the general RudiB/amazing HOE thread or the Lighting thread. Ahh, here goes anyway.

Over the weekend I found a somewhat serious flaw in my latest P-51 hologram. When I tilted the top of the hologram towards me a number of interesting serpentine shapes leapt out of the surface of the film. I figured I'd missed a mount in my carding off and set about finding it. What I found instead was that the far edge of my master glass was reflecting light directly onto the copy plate. Because that edge had a somewhat uneven break it was creating interesting shapes.

Something to think about when creating a non-traditional display hologram (IE, one that tries to break out of the copy-of-an-object box) is to work in all different kinds of reflection and refraction to create unique/interesting shapes in the final hologram.

Michael, I would not worry about keeping threads on the topic they are started as unless it strays completely off subject, it will drive you nuts as a lot of holography posts leads us to think of something different. And as far as the topic goes, that is part of the thread.

Anyway, there was someone on the old forum that mentioned the same thing although I am not sure if he nailed down what the culprit was. But he liked the effect so much he wanted to make them on purpose. I have also seen it in one of my bottle holograms. Because the bottle was in a mirror box, at very severe angles you could see the edge of the mirror box (glass edge) and it created a zig zag patteren of light. I covered the edge with black tape on subsiquent shots but the effect was pretty neat.
